Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test case `testLANG571()` expects that calling `ArrayUtils.add()` with both parameters `array` and `element` null throws an `IllegalArgumentException`. The current implementation of `ArrayUtils.add(T[] array, T element)` does not perform any null-check to throw such an exception. 

Instead, it determines the type to use for a new array as follows:
- If `array` is not null: use `array.getClass()`.
- Else if `element` is not null: use `element.getClass()`.
- Else (both null): use `Object.class`.

Then it calls `copyArrayGrow1(array, type)`. Inside `copyArrayGrow1`, since `array` is null, a new array of `newArrayComponentType` of length 1 is created. Here, it will create an `Object[]` array because `newArrayComponentType` is `Object.class`.

Finally, `add()` stores the `element` (which is null in this test) in the new array and returns it.

As a result, the returned array is of type `Object[]`. The test code expects to assign this to `String[]` which causes a `ClassCastException` because an `Object[]` cannot be cast to `String[]`.

The bug report precisely points out this unexpected `ClassCastException` when both array and element are null. The test expects an `IllegalArgumentException` but no such check exists.

The root cause is that the method has no validation to prohibit both inputs being null which leads to an array of `Object[]` being created and then fails at runtime due to a type mismatch during assignment.

Recent bug reports are unrelated to this issue.

Therefore, the fix should add a validation that throws `IllegalArgumentException` if both `array` and `element` are null, to match the test expectation and prevent the unexpected `ClassCastException`.

This explains the failure of `testLANG571()` which expects an exception on null parameters but gets a `ClassCastException` instead.
org.apache.commons.lang3.ArrayUtils.add(T[], T)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
